movie_title_en: L’Oréal Paris: ‘Le Défilé’ Live from Paris Fashion Week
synopsis:
AS OFFICIAL PARTNER OF THE PARIS FASHION WEEK, L’ORÉAL PARIS WILL HOST ITS ANNUAL PUBLIC RUNWAY SHOW IN FRONT OF THE EIFFEL TOWER, IN CELEBRATION OF WOMEN’S EMPOWERMENT.

On September 28th at 9pm EST (8pm BST), Place Joffre will transform into an open-air stage where beauty, fashion and self-expression come together. Set between the Eiffel Tower and the École Militaire, L'Oréal Paris' iconic public runway show invites women to Express Their Worth, celebrating women’s empowerment, inclusivity, freedom, confidence and sisterhood.

For the ninth time since 2017, Le Défilé L’Oréal Paris will celebrate sisterhood and the synergy between state-of-the-art beauty expertise and fashion, featuring global make-up artist Harold James and hair expert Stéphane Lancien.

Exclusive Everyman Screening Perks
- Welcome drink upon arrival
- 60-minute, pre-show cocktail reception from 7pm
- A special surprise musical guest during the event
- An exclusive money-can't-buy goodie bag featuring L'Oréal Paris products (worth over £75)

Featuring a Star-Studded Catwalk Line-Up with; Simone Ashley, Marie Bochet, Viola Davis, Cara Delevingne, Jane Fonda, Bebe Vio Grandis, Ariana Greenblatt, Luma Grothe, Kendall Jenner, Aja Naomi King, Eva Longoria, Andie MacDowell, Aishwarya Rai, and newly appointed ambassador Kristen Bell.

synopsis:
On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Népstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. 

Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favourite tracks— "Bohemian Rhapsody,” "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Free” and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country’s top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity.
